title: Sonic & Mascot Platformers
blurb: The blue blur and the roster of speed-obsessed rivals Sega built around him, defining the Mega Drive's whole personality.

games.title: Sonic the Hedgehog
games.blurb: The pack-in that reinvented Sega overnight: loop-de-loops, spin-dashes, and a level of speed the NES generation had never felt.

games.title: Sonic the Hedgehog 2
games.blurb: Tails joins in, the Spin Dash arrives, and Emerald Hill Zone becomes the platform's signature opening act.

games.title: Sonic the Hedgehog 3
games.blurb: A darker, denser Sonic with save files, elemental shields, and Knuckles crashing in as a genuine rival.

games.title: Sonic & Knuckles
games.blurb: The lock-on cartridge that let the console physically merge two games into one sprawling adventure.

games.title: Ristar
games.blurb: A late-era gem built around a stretchy-armed star-child who grabs and headbutts his way through gorgeous, painterly worlds.

games.title: Dynamite Headdy
games.blurb: A puppet-theatre platformer overflowing with ideas, where the hero's detachable head becomes the whole toolkit.

games.title: Alex Kidd in the Enchanted Castle
games.blurb: Sega's original mascot before Sonic, swapping punches and rock-paper-scissors duels through a fairy-tale kingdom.

games.title: Rocket Knight Adventures
games.blurb: A jetpack-propelled opossum knight in armor, charging and boosting through some of the era's most kinetic level design.

games.title: Vectorman
games.blurb: A shape-shifting robot soldier rendered with pre-rendered 3D sprites, wringing striking visuals out of the aging hardware.

games.title: Kid Chameleon
games.blurb: A sprawling, mask-swapping platformer that hands the player dozens of power-up forms across a genuinely huge map.

title: Licensed & Platforming Icons
blurb: Disney deals and Western studio talent turned cartoon licenses into some of the console's most polished platforming.

games.title: Earthworm Jim
games.blurb: A super-suited earthworm swinging his own detached head as a whip, animated with a cartoon lunacy few games matched.

games.title: Earthworm Jim 2
games.blurb: Stranger, funnier, and more inventive than the original, trading straight platforming for a string of bizarre mini-concepts.

games.title: QuackShot starring Donald Duck
games.blurb: An Indiana Jones pastiche starring Donald on a globe-trotting treasure hunt, built on genuine exploration and backtracking.

games.title: Disney's Aladdin
games.blurb: Hand-animated by former Disney artists, with a sword-slashing, apple-throwing Aladdin that still looks remarkable today.

games.title: Castle of Illusion Starring Mickey Mouse
games.blurb: A launch-era showcase of what the hardware could do with a storybook world and a bounce-happy Mickey.

games.title: World of Illusion Starring Mickey Mouse and Donald Duck
games.blurb: A two-player follow-up pairing Mickey and Donald through a shared magical adventure, co-op done early and well.

games.title: Cool Spot
games.blurb: The 7-Up mascot's own outing, built by the Aladdin team into a tight, atmospheric beach-side platformer.

games.title: James Pond II: Codename RoboCod
games.blurb: A British spy-fish comedy platformer whose stretching, telescoping body became its signature puzzle mechanic.

games.title: Taz-Mania
games.blurb: The whirlwind-spinning Looney Tunes devil chews, spins, and rampages through an unusually chaotic platformer.

games.title: Puggsy
games.blurb: An underappreciated British puzzle-platformer where a stranded alien solves rooms by picking up and hurling nearly everything.

title: Beat-'Em-Ups & Brawlers
blurb: The genre the Mega Drive made its own: street gangs, ancient armies, and rubber-suited turtles, all cleared out fist by fist.

games.title: Streets of Rage
games.blurb: A synth-heavy debut that set the template for the console's signature brawler series.

games.title: Streets of Rage 2
games.blurb: Widely considered the genre's high point, with Yuzo Koshiro's soundtrack and a roster everyone remembers.

games.title: Streets of Rage 3
games.blurb: A faster, stranger, more experimental close to the trilogy, leaning into dashes, blitz attacks, and a darker plot.

games.title: Golden Axe
games.blurb: Sword-and-sorcery brawling with rideable beasts and a magic meter, translating the arcade hit onto cartridge.

games.title: Golden Axe II
games.blurb: A cartridge-exclusive sequel that leaned harder into spectacle, with bigger magic effects and a longer campaign.

games.title: Altered Beast
games.blurb: The console's original pack-in, where a resurrected warrior transforms into werewolves and dragons to rescue Athena.

games.title: Comix Zone
games.blurb: A brawler drawn as a living comic book, where the hero punches his way panel to panel through his own pages.

games.title: Mazin Saga: Mutant Fighter
games.blurb: A giant-robot brawler built on the Mazinger anime license, mixing beat-'em-up combat with fighting-game specials.

games.title: Teenage Mutant Hero Turtles: The Hyperstone Heist
games.blurb: Europe's censor-friendly Turtles rename for a tight, arcade-faithful four-turtle brawl through familiar city streets.

title: Run-and-Gun & Action
blurb: Fast, loud, and frequently punishing — the console's answer to the arcade's most trigger-happy genre.

games.title: Gunstar Heroes
games.blurb: Treasure's debut and a genre landmark, stacking weapon combinations and boss gauntlets at a relentless pace.

games.title: Alien Soldier
games.blurb: Nearly wall-to-wall boss fights, built around a rapid weapon-switching system that rewards mastery over memorization.

games.title: Ranger X
games.blurb: A mech-riding shooter that lets the player leap on and off a giant hover-bike mid-battle.

games.title: Target Earth
games.blurb: An early mech-combat game with a deliberate, tactical pace closer to a simulation than a shooter.

games.title: Probotector
games.blurb: Europe's robot-reskinned edition of the run-and-gun classic, swapping human soldiers for droids to sidestep content rules.

games.title: Shinobi III: Return of the Ninja Master
games.blurb: A ninja action game built on pure momentum, with a run button that turns every stage into a sprint.

games.title: Mercs
games.blurb: A top-down commando shoot-'em-up ported from the arcade, playable solo or with a friend.

games.title: Cyborg Justice
games.blurb: A part-brawler, part-shooter where the hero rebuilds himself from scavenged robot parts as he fights.

title: Shoot-'Em-Ups
blurb: Technosoft, Toaplan, and Compile brought arcade-grade bullet-dodging home, several of these titles collector's-market legends.

games.title: Thunder Force III
games.blurb: Never officially released in Europe, but a defining side-scrolling shooter with selectable stage order and a beloved soundtrack.

games.title: Thunder Force IV
games.blurb: Kept its Thunder Force name in Europe while North America renamed it Lightening Force: Quest for the Darkstar.

games.title: M.U.S.H.A.
games.blurb: A vertical shooter with no European release, but treasured by shooter fans for its density and difficulty curve.

games.title: Gleylancer
games.blurb: A Japan-only vertical shooter with a rotating multi-directional shot system that outclassed much of its competition.

games.title: Truxton
games.blurb: A tightly-designed vertical shooter from Toaplan's arcade pedigree, ported faithfully to cartridge.

games.title: Elemental Master
games.blurb: Never released in Europe, this fantasy-themed shooter pairs elemental magic spells with traditional bullet patterns.

games.title: Zero Wing
games.blurb: A side-scrolling shooter better known today for its garbled opening cutscene than for its genuinely solid combat.

games.title: Bio-Hazard Battle
games.blurb: An organic, creature-piloted shooter with a distinctly biological art style rare among its peers.

games.title: Sub-Terrania
games.blurb: A gravity-driven cavern shooter demanding precise thrust control as much as trigger reflexes.

games.title: Steel Empire
games.blurb: A steampunk shooter of airships and biplanes, later remembered as one of the more visually distinctive entries in the genre.

title: Role-Playing Adventures
blurb: From Sega's own Phantasy Star lineage to cult European favorites, the Mega Drive's RPG library rewards patient exploring.

games.title: Phantasy Star II
games.blurb: A dramatic leap from its 8-bit predecessor, with a grim story and a science-fantasy setting years ahead of its time.

games.title: Phantasy Star III: Generations of Doom
games.blurb: A generational saga where marriage choices ripple forward across three playable eras of the same family line.

games.title: Phantasy Star IV: The End of the Millennium
games.blurb: A late-cycle showcase for the series, pairing comic-panel cutscenes with some of the deepest combat on the console.

games.title: Shining Force
games.blurb: A tactical RPG that made grid-based army building approachable, with a huge cast to recruit and train.

games.title: Shining Force II
games.blurb: A bigger, more polished sequel that many still consider the high point of Mega Drive tactics games.

games.title: Shining in the Darkness
games.blurb: A first-person dungeon crawler from the same team, trading army tactics for corridor-by-corridor exploration.

games.title: Landstalker: The Treasures of King Nole
games.blurb: An isometric action-RPG built on precise jumping puzzles as much as combat, with a wry sense of humor throughout.

games.title: The Story of Thor
games.blurb: Europe's title for the action-RPG North America knew as Beyond Oasis, built around elemental spirit companions.

games.title: Soleil
games.blurb: Europe's name for the game North America called Crusader of Centy, an animal-transforming action-RPG in a Zelda-adjacent mold.

games.title: Shadowrun
games.blurb: Never released in Europe, this cyberpunk-fantasy RPG adapts the tabletop setting into a genuinely ambitious action-RPG.

title: Strategy & Simulation
blurb: War games, god games, and everything in between, several imported by British studios who understood the genre best.

games.title: Herzog Zwei
games.blurb: Widely credited as a genuine ancestor of the real-time strategy genre, commanding units from a transforming mech.

games.title: General Chaos
games.blurb: A squad-based tactics game played for slapstick comedy as much as strategy, with cartoonish soldier chaos.

games.title: Populous
games.blurb: The original god game, terraforming land and guiding followers in a genre Peter Molyneux's team effectively invented.

games.title: Dune II: The Battle for Arrakis
games.blurb: Europe's cartridge title for the console adaptation of the game that helped define modern real-time strategy, distinct from the PC original.

games.title: Warsong
games.blurb: Never released in Europe, this is the North American localization of Japan's Langrisser, a foundational tactical RPG.

games.title: Gain Ground
games.blurb: An overhead action-strategy hybrid where rescued units carry forward, forcing careful squad management across eras.

games.title: Master of Monsters
games.blurb: Never released in Europe, this turn-based fantasy strategy game pits summoned monster armies against rival lords.

title: Puzzle
blurb: Falling blocks and quick-thinking arcade puzzles, several of them Sega's own answer to the Tetris craze.

games.title: Columns
games.blurb: Sega's own falling-gem answer to Tetris, simple enough to become an unofficial pack-in classic.

games.title: Dr. Robotnik's Mean Bean Machine
games.blurb: A reskinned Puyo Puyo starring Sonic's villain, and one of the sharpest competitive puzzlers on the console.

games.title: Klax
games.blurb: An arcade conveyor-belt puzzler about catching and sorting colored tiles before they hit the floor.

games.title: Pac-Panic
games.blurb: Europe's name for the falling-block puzzler North America released a year later as Pac-Attack.

games.title: Zoop
games.blurb: A frantic shape-matching puzzler where colored shapes creep in from the edges and must be cleared before they reach center.

games.title: Mega Bomberman
games.blurb: A console-exclusive Bomberman built around a sprawling single-player quest alongside the usual multiplayer mayhem.

title: Sports
blurb: EA's Mega Drive sports run built the template modern sports games still follow, alongside a few gleefully strange detours.

games.title: Mutant League Football
games.blurb: American football with land mines, skeleton linemen, and a sense of humor sports games rarely allow themselves.

games.title: Mutant League Hockey
games.blurb: The gridiron formula reapplied to the rink, keeping the chaos and adding blood-soaked ice.

games.title: Super Baseball 2020
games.blurb: A future-set baseball game with robots on the roster, an odd but memorable arcade conversion.

games.title: Zany Golf
games.blurb: Miniature golf reimagined as a physics playground, full of windmills, ramps, and genuinely clever course design.

games.title: NHL '94
games.blurb: Still cited by hockey fans as one of the tightest, most responsive sports games ever made on any hardware.

games.title: John Madden Football '93
games.blurb: A key early entry in the Madden lineage, refining the formula that would define EA Sports for decades.

games.title: WWF Royal Rumble
games.blurb: A wrestling game built around the chaotic multi-man Royal Rumble format rather than one-on-one bouts.

title: Racing
blurb: British studios Codemasters and Bitmap-adjacent teams gave the Mega Drive a distinctly European flavor of speed.

games.title: Micro Machines
games.blurb: Toy-car racing across kitchen tables and garden hoses, from a British studio that made the license genuinely great.

games.title: Micro Machines 2: Turbo Tournament
games.blurb: A refined sequel adding new toy-scale locations and one of the console's best multiplayer split-screen setups.

games.title: Super Monaco GP
games.blurb: An arcade-accurate Formula One conversion with a surprisingly deep season mode for the era.

games.title: Road Rash
games.blurb: Motorcycle racing where punching and kicking rivals off their bikes is just as important as the finish line.

games.title: Rock N' Roll Racing
games.blurb: An isometric combat-racer from the future Blizzard team, packed with rock riffs and weaponized vehicles.

games.title: OutRun
games.blurb: The arcade's breezy coastal cruiser brought home, trading route forks and a stereo soundtrack for pure driving feel.

games.title: Combat Cars
games.blurb: A vehicular-combat racer built for split-screen mayhem well before that became a genre unto itself.

title: Fighting
blurb: The console's fighting-game answer to the arcade boom, from home-grown brawlers to divisive ports of the era's biggest hits.

games.title: Eternal Champions
games.blurb: Sega's own attempt at a flagship fighter, with a cast of time-displaced warriors and gruesome finishing moves.

games.title: Mortal Kombat
games.blurb: The uncensored, blood-intact home port that made the Mega Drive the system fighting fans reached for first.

games.title: Mortal Kombat II
games.blurb: A stronger, more complete conversion of the arcade sequel, again keeping the violence the SNES version cut.

games.title: WeaponLord
games.blurb: Never released in Europe, this deep, technical fighter arrived late but earned a small, devoted following.

games.title: Teenage Mutant Hero Turtles: Tournament Fighters
games.blurb: Europe's Turtles-branded one-on-one fighter, distinct from and often preferred over its SNES and NES counterparts.

games.title: King of the Monsters
games.blurb: A giant-monster wrestling game translating SNK's arcade kaiju brawl onto cartridge.

title: Cult Classics & European Curios
blurb: The console's British and French developer scene left a distinct fingerprint here, in games this collection's European framing was built to celebrate.

games.title: ToeJam & Earl
games.blurb: Two funky aliens exploring a randomly generated Earth, blending roguelike structure with a laid-back groove.

games.title: ToeJam & Earl in Panic on Funkotron
games.blurb: A more conventional platforming sequel, trading procedural exploration for tighter, level-based design.

games.title: Flashback: The Quest for Identity
games.blurb: A French rotoscoped sci-fi adventure of cinematic platforming and amnesia-driven mystery.

games.title: Cannon Fodder
games.blurb: A darkly comic overhead war game where each fallen soldier gets a cross on the title-screen hillside.

games.title: Zombies Ate My Neighbors
games.blurb: A horror-comedy shooter rescuing hapless neighbors from a checklist of B-movie monsters.

games.title: Alisia Dragoon
games.blurb: A lightning-whip action game with a striking pixel-art style and a roster of dragon familiars to summon.

games.title: Speedball 2: Brutal Deluxe
games.blurb: A violent, futuristic sport blending handball and hockey, still cited as one of the genre's finest.

games.title: Xenon 2: Megablast
games.blurb: A vertical shooter built around a shop system for upgrading the ship between runs, with a Bomb the Bass soundtrack.

games.title: The Chaos Engine
games.blurb: Known in North America as Soldiers of Fortune, a steampunk co-op shooter through a Victorian nightmare landscape.

games.title: Lemmings
games.blurb: The console conversion of DMA Design's puzzle phenomenon, guiding waves of doomed little walkers to safety.
